title: What to Wear to a Tamil Wedding as a Guest (Muhurtham & Reception)
excerpt: What to wear to a Tamil wedding as a female guest: silk sarees and silk-look kurta sets for the muhurtham and reception, the best colours, colours to avoid and styling tips.
seo_title: Tamil Wedding Guest Outfit 2026: What to Wear to 4 Functions
seo_description: Muhurtham, reception & 2 more: what female guests wear, lucky colours, colours to avoid and non-saree looks – all in one quick table.
body:
## Quick answer

At a Tamil wedding, female guests traditionally wear a **silk saree, often a Kanchipuram (Kanjivaram) silk**, in rich colours like **mustard, magenta, emerald, maroon or peacock blue**. A silk-look **kurta set or Anarkali** is perfectly acceptable if you do not wear sarees. The main ceremony, the **muhurtham**, is often early in the morning at a temple or wedding hall, so plan a respectful, covered outfit. Avoid **all black** and **plain white**, and add **jasmine flowers** to your hair if you like.

This guide is for guests attending Tamil weddings in India, Sri Lanka, the UK, Canada, the US, Singapore or Malaysia.

## What are the functions at a Tamil wedding?

| Function | When | What to wear | Colours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nichayathartham (engagement) | Weeks or a day before | Silk saree or chanderi kurta set | Soft or rich colours |
| Reception | Often the evening **before** the muhurtham | Your most glamorous outfit | Jewel tones, gold, pastels with shine |
| Nalangu and pre-wedding rituals | Day before | Light silk or cotton | Bright, cheerful |
| Muhurtham (main ceremony) | Early morning, often 6–10 am | Silk saree or silk-look kurta set | Mustard, magenta, green, maroon, peacock blue |

Unlike many North Indian weddings, the reception at a Tamil wedding is often held the night before the main ceremony. Check the invitation carefully.

## What should you wear to the muhurtham?

The muhurtham is the auspicious moment when the groom ties the thaali (mangalsutra) around the bride's neck. It usually takes place in the morning at a temple or a kalyana mandapam (wedding hall).

- **Traditional:** a Kanchipuram silk saree with a contrast border, or a lighter silk-cotton saree.
- **If you do not wear sarees:** a silk-look kurta set with a dupatta, or an Anarkali in a rich colour. Chanderi and taffeta silk give the sheen of silk without the weight.
- **Coverage:** keep shoulders covered and avoid short hemlines, especially in a temple.
- **Shoes:** you will remove them at the temple or mandapam entrance.

The [sage green taffeta silk Anarkali](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/) ($52) gives the richness of silk for close family friends.

## Which colours should you wear to a Tamil wedding?

Tamil weddings love bright, auspicious colours. Guests usually choose:

- **Mustard and turmeric yellow:** auspicious and very traditional.
- **Magenta and rani pink:** festive and photogenic.
- **Emerald, bottle green and parrot green:** classic Kanchipuram shades.
- **Maroon and deep red-brown:** rich and traditional (avoid a bright bridal red head to toe).
- **Peacock blue and royal blue:** striking in photos.
- **Contrast borders:** a gold or contrast-coloured border is very much in style.

### Colours to avoid

- **All black:** considered inauspicious at many Tamil weddings.
- **Plain white:** associated with mourning. White or cream with a gold border, as in a Kerala-style saree, is different and may be fine – ask if unsure.
- **Head-to-toe bridal red:** leave that to the bride.

## What should you wear to a Tamil wedding reception?

The reception is the glamorous evening event. Guests wear heavier silk sarees, designer sarees, lehengas or Anarkalis. This is the moment for shine and embroidery.

The [royal blue georgette Anarkali with gota dupatta](/products/royal-blue-georgette-anarkali-suit-gota-handwork-dupatta/) ($52) or the [lavender taffeta silk Anarkali](/products/lavender-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-organza-dupatta/) ($52) both work well under evening lights.

## Styling a Tamil wedding guest look

1. **Jasmine flowers (malli poo):** a string of jasmine in a braid or bun is a lovely, traditional touch.
2. **Gold-tone jewellery:** temple jewellery, jhumkas or a simple necklace suits the occasion.
3. **A small bindi:** if you usually wear one.
4. **Comfortable footwear:** you will slip them off often.
5. **Light layers:** morning ceremonies in India can be warm, while UK and Canadian halls can be cold.

## Sri Lankan Tamil weddings in the UK and Canada

Sri Lankan Tamil weddings in London, Toronto and elsewhere follow many of the same traditions: a morning ceremony, rich silk sarees and bright, auspicious colours. The reception is often a separate evening event at a banqueting hall. The same colour rules apply.

## What should a non-Tamil guest wear?

You do not need a Kanchipuram saree. A silk-look kurta set or Anarkali in mustard, magenta, green or blue, with covered shoulders, is respectful and elegant. Hosts are usually delighted when guests wear Indian clothes.

## Frequently asked questions

**What should I wear to a Tamil wedding as a guest?**
A silk saree, ideally Kanchipuram silk, or a silk-look kurta set or Anarkali in mustard, magenta, emerald, maroon or peacock blue. Keep shoulders covered for the morning ceremony.

**Can I wear a kurta set instead of a saree to a Tamil wedding?**
Yes. A chanderi or silk-look kurta set with a dupatta, or an Anarkali, is perfectly acceptable for guests.

**What colours should I avoid at a Tamil wedding?**
Avoid all black, plain white and head-to-toe bridal red.

**What time is a Tamil wedding ceremony?**
The muhurtham is usually in the early morning, often between 6 and 10 am, at an auspicious time chosen by the family. The reception is often held the evening before.

**Should I wear flowers in my hair to a Tamil wedding?**
It is not required, but a string of jasmine is a lovely, traditional touch that hosts appreciate.

**What should I wear to a Tamil wedding reception?**
A heavier silk saree, a lehenga or a glamorous Anarkali with embroidery or shine.
